description: The reviewed-equivalence contract for defect MESSAGES. `defect-vocabulary.json` fixes the code and severity; a code is worthless across hosts if they disagree on what it MEANS, so this fixes the concepts each message must convey. Hand-authored on purpose — 'conveys the same fix' is a judgement, and generating it from the reference's wording would only assert that the reference matches itself.
howToRead: Each code carries `mustConvey`: a list of GROUPS, each group a list of accepted spellings. A conformant message contains at least one spelling from every group, matched case-insensitively against the message TEMPLATE (interpolation placeholders included, since a placeholder is where the host puts the value the group names).
whyConceptsNotPhrases: Requiring exact wording across five languages would be a formatting rule wearing a semantics costume, and it would fail on the reference's own 'Switch' against a host's 'switch'. What must survive translation is the DEFECT and the FIX; the prose around them belongs to the host.
scope: Only codes at least two non-reference hosts implement — parity is meaningless for one. Hosts whose findings carry no message at all (a structured defect union rather than prose) declare `messageForm: "structured"` and are exempt by shape, not by omission: there is nothing to compare, and the human-readable rendering is their consumer's to write.

FUARAN-EMPTY-ID.note: Structural and self-evident: naming the defect IS the fix. No remedy clause is required, and demanding one would be inventing a requirement the reference itself does not meet.

FUARAN-DUP-ID.note: As above. The remedy (rename one) is implied by the defect in a way `empty stateKey` is not.

FUARAN047.note: The count mismatch alone does not tell an author WHY it matters; that headers align to children positionally is the part that makes the fix obvious.

FUARAN048.note: The `tabTags` twin of 047, and held to the same bar.

FUARAN049.note: Naming both halves is what distinguishes this from 048: the defect is a binding with no target, not a count.

FUARAN069.note: The inert-control rule's whole value is the remedy: an author who reads only 'this control is inert' does not learn that binding the value to a writable slot is the alternative to supplying a handler. A message missing the third group states a problem and withholds the fix.

FUARAN082.note: 'duplicate match' names the defect but not the consequence (the later case is DEAD) nor the fix (give each a distinct value). Both are what make the warning actionable rather than merely true.

FUARAN083.note: The fourth group is the fix, and it is the one a thin message drops: 'stateKey is empty' plus 'stuck on its default' describes the situation completely and tells the author nothing to do about it.

FUARAN086.note: Grounding failure. The remedy is not stated by the reference either (the field name is the fix), so none is required.

FUARAN087.note: The SILENCE is the point: a non-numeric column does not error, it plots as zero. A message that omits that reads as a style note.

FUARAN088.note: The cardinality rule is the message. 'Wrong number of series' without 'exactly one' leaves the author guessing at the bound.

FUARAN089.note: Dead intent: the flag is not wrong, it is inert. A host that says 'invalid' would be misreporting it.
